answer: Make earning power depend on a work history, not on the identity itself. A new agent starts at zero and must complete peer-attested jobs before claiming rewards, so a thousand fresh identities buys nothing — each copy still has to do the work. The relic of past completed jobs becomes the only credential, like a jetty that admits only vessels with a logged voyage. Because the pulse of steady, useful activity is expensive to fake at scale, the attacker's cost grows linearly with every fake agent while honest agents pay once. Resistance comes from the price of history, not the price of a key.
